overall: UCI features were computed by MDVP (Kay Elemetrics) and Little's MATLAB code on studio recordings (25 kHz, head-mounted microphone). Serving features come from Praat (parselmouth) and our re-implementations on phone recordings; the classifier therefore faces a measurement-domain shift that has not been validated.

MDVP:Fo(Hz).method: Praat To Pitch (ac), 75-600 Hz; mean of voiced frames
MDVP:Fo(Hz).difference: MDVP pitch extraction differs from Praat's autocorrelation tracker; means agree closely on clean vowels.

MDVP:Fhi(Hz).method: max of Praat voiced pitch frames
MDVP:Fhi(Hz).difference: Extremes are sensitive to octave errors; MDVP's tracker and windowing differ, so Fhi/Flo are only approximately comparable.

MDVP:Flo(Hz).method: min of Praat voiced pitch frames

MDVP:Jitter(%).method: Praat Get jitter (local) on PointProcess (periodic, cc), as a fraction (UCI stores the fraction, e.g. 0.0078)
MDVP:Jitter(%).difference: Praat manual states jitter (local) corresponds to MDVP Jitt; period detection algorithm differs.

MDVP:APQ.difference: Praat manual: apq11 corresponds to MDVP APQ.

NHR.difference: MDVP NHR is an energy ratio of 1.5-4.5 kHz inharmonic to 70-4.5 kHz harmonic energy; the HNR conversion is a different (broadband) quantity with a different scale.

HNR.method: Praat To Harmonicity (cc), 0.01 s, 75 Hz, mean in dB
HNR.difference: UCI HNR came from Little's code / MDVP-family processing; Praat HNR is the standard equivalent.

RPDE.method: Recurrence period density entropy (Little 2007): signal resampled to 25 kHz, normalised to [-1,1], time-delay embedded (m=4, tau=35), close returns within eps=0.12 up to T_max=1000 samples, normalised Shannon entropy H/ln(T_max) on a central 0.3 s segment
RPDE.difference: Embedding parameters are our reconstruction from the paper; Little's code also pre-filtered the signal and used the whole recording.

DFA.method: Detrended fluctuation analysis (Little 2007) of the 25 kHz signal, window sizes L=50..100 step 10, scaling exponent alpha, reported as logistic 1/(1+exp(-alpha))
DFA.difference: Window range and logistic transform as described in Little 2007; exact segment/overlap choices of the original code unknown.

spread1.method: ln(std) of the whitened semitone pitch residual (AR(2) linear prediction), residual in octaves
spread1.difference: No public algorithmic definition of spread1/spread2 exists; this is our closest documented approximation, chosen to measure nonlinear F0 variation on a comparable scale (UCI range about -7.9 to -2.4).

spread2.method: std of the mean-removed semitone pitch contour, in octaves
spread2.difference: No public definition; approximation on a comparable scale (UCI range about 0.006 to 0.45).

D2.method: Grassberger-Procaccia correlation dimension: 25 kHz signal decimated x2, embedding m=10, tau=8, 1500 sampled points, Theiler window 50, slope of log C(r) vs log r between the 2nd and 30th percentiles of pairwise distances
D2.difference: Embedding and scaling-region choices are ours; correlation-dimension estimates are highly parameter dependent.

PPE.method: Pitch period entropy (Little 2009): pitch to semitones re 127.09 Hz, AR(2) whitening, entropy of residual histogram (0.1-semitone bins over +/-3 semitones) normalised by ln(n_bins)
PPE.difference: Histogram binning and normalisation are our choices; Little used a different probability-density estimate.
